subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO, KMS/HSM & log retention
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging) — next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the call today — good to meet you and Priya. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of FintechCo requirements we discussed:
- SSO: SAML-based SSO (Okta) for all user access; SCIM user sync preferred.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys required; preference for HSM-backed KMS (AWS CloudHSM / dedicated HSM) for encryption of customer data at rest.
- Logging & retention: security/audit logs must be retained for 7 years and shipped to FintechCo-managed storage (S3) and to Splunk. No log data should be retained beyond that policy.
- Network: no public-internet egress for sensitive payloads; private VPC connectivity or on-prem option strongly preferred.

Why this matters for deployment mode: 
- Hosted API (our standard) is fastest but does not support customer-controlled HSM and by default uses Redwood-managed KMS. Datasets traverse our hosted control plane and public endpoints — likely insufficient for your compliance needs.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) can provide tenant isolation and VPC peering, and supports integration with customer KMS in many cases, but HSM-backed keys are limited depending on cloud provider setup — needs confirmation.
- Private deployment (VPC-on premises or air-gapped) gives the strongest guarantees: customer-managed KMS/HSM, private networking, and full control over log retention/shipping.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you share the IT/security requirements spreadsheet you mentioned (SAML metadata, KMS/HSM details, SIEM endpoints)?
2) I’d like to get Rishi (solutions architect) and Neha (CS) on a technical follow-up with your infra/security leads to go through connectivity and KMS specifics.
3) Please share expected throughput (rps and tokens/day) so we can size Dedicated if that ends up being the right fit.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (high-level diff Hosted/Dedicated/Private), security-checklist.pdf

If Wed or Thu next week works for a technical deep-dive, propose a couple slots and we’ll coordinate.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging) — next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SSO: Yes, Okta SAML + SCIM for provisioning. We can provide SAML metadata and a SCIM endpoint spec.
- KMS/HSM: Compliance requires HSM-backed keys for the production encryption envelope. We run in AWS and use AWS KMS with CloudHSM for key material. If Dedicated can integrate with our KMS and HSM in a way that the key never leaves our control, that would be acceptable. Otherwise we will need a Private deployment.
- Logging/Retention: We need immutable audit logs retained for 7 years and forwarded to our S3 bucket and Splunk indexer. Logs must not be accessible by third parties.
- Network: No production traffic should route over public internet — we prefer VPC-only peering or an on-prem connector.

I attached our IT requirements workbook (FintechCo_IT_requirements.xlsx) with the sections your team requested.

We are leaning toward Private but open to Dedicated if you can confirm HSM support and end-to-end private networking.

For the technical deep dive: Wed Dec 2 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu Dec 3 9:00-10:00 PT — either works for our infra lead (Priya). Can Rishi join the Wed slot?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure | FintechCo
alex.johnson@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment constraints (SSO / KMS / logging) — next steps

Alex — thanks for the detail and for the workbook. I reviewed it and pulled together the high-level tradeoffs so your team can prep for the technical call: 

Quick tradeoff summary: 
- Hosted API: Pros = fastest to go-live, managed upgrades, minimal ops. Cons = Redwood-managed KMS, public endpoints, not compatible with HSM-backed keys or strict VPC-only requirements.
- Dedicated capacity: Pros = isolated GPU pools, VPC peering/PrivateLink for traffic, can often integrate with customer KMS via cross-account grants. Cons = HSM-backed key support depends on cloud networking and whether CloudHSM is provisioned in the same account/VPC — in many cases we can support it but we need your cloud security to confirm allowed network/topology and key import policies.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Pros = supports customer-managed KMS/HSM (keys stay in your HSM), private-only networking, full control over log storage and retention. Cons = longer lead time for provisioning and ops coordination.

What Rishi and I will cover on the call:
- Detailed KMS/HSM integration patterns we’ve done (cross-account AWS KMS grants vs. on-prem HSM).
- Network architectures: VPC peering, PrivateLink, and on-prem connector options.
- Log shipping: S3 + Splunk ingestion patterns, retention enforcement, and encryption-in-transit.
- Sizing questions: please bring expected request rate and typical token lengths so we can model Dedicated sizing and cost if needed.

We can confirm that Private deployments are the only path that guarantees HSM-backed keys with zero-key-extractability from Redwood-managed infrastructure. Dedicated can often meet your needs but will require an architecture review and likely CloudHSM setup in your account.

Wed Dec 2 10:00 PT works for Rishi and me — we’ll send a calendar invite for a 60-minute technical session and include our security architect. Could you please invite your security lead as well?

Attaching a short note on KMS/HSM patterns (redwood-kms-hsm-quicknote.pdf). We’ll review the workbook on the call and capture any redlines for the deployment plan.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
